new.n: Hermit Pritchard's cache, Flynn Island, Higgins Lake
new.pl: GNIS Flynn Island ('Hermit Island', later 'Treasure Island'), Higgins Lake; about 30 acres, now cottage lots
new.v: Civil War bounty money (legend; no amount)
new.st: Israel 'Ezra' Porter Pritchard lived about twenty years as a hermit on Flynn Island ('Hermit Island', later 'Treasure Island') in Higgins Lake. He was found dead in his dugout in 1902 and buried in the potter's field of the Roscommon cemetery. The tale says he buried Civil War bounty-jumper money somewhere on the roughly 30-acre island; no amount is given and nothing was ever found.
new.t: A descendant posting online denies the bounty-money story; no period paper yet mentions a cache. The island is built over with cottages: look only. A 1902 Roscommon or Grayling death notice is being sought.
pinev: GNIS Flynn Island, Higgins Lake; the circle covers the island, the cache spot is unknown.
new.tovw: Lead grade D (treasure thread): late secondary telling only, disputed by a descendant

set.st: French trader Joseph Bertrand, founder of Bertrand (4 mi S of Niles), sold land and buried "a full bushel of gold and silver coins" from fear of robbers, then forgot the spot; he believed it was under an apple tree in his orchard. Hundreds searched; "every foot of the orchard" was dug by 1898-99. Pin is between his 1873 house lot and estate, not the spot itself. The earliest print found is the Green Bay Press-Gazette of 12 Dec 1898; the wire then ran in Indiana, Ohio, Illinois and New Jersey from 15 Dec, and the first Michigan print found is 28 Dec 1898. A Niles Daily Star line (5 Dec 1898) once read as saying no one locally had heard of the tale is unverified: the page hit may be an advertisement, and the Niles papers of early 1899 are being checked.
src: Niles Daily Star 5 Dec 1898 p3 (newspapers.com 1020495798, PC (a)): UNVERIFIED, the hit may be a baking-powder ad
Green Bay Press-Gazette, 12 Dec 1898, p. 10 (Newspapers.com 187615897): earliest print found; ran in IN/OH/IL/NJ from 15 Dec
Livingston County Daily Press and Argus, 28 Dec 1898, p. 7 (Newspapers.com 453547931): first Michigan print found
North Iowa Times (McGregor), 20 Jul 1905, p. 1 (reprinting the Crawford Co. Press): four bags; soldier 'Mercierre'; 'highest point across from' where found
Dubuque Herald, 12 Mar 1922, p. 2: $50,000 in a keg in the woods W of the 'government barn' (Pike) on the old military road near the Quarter Way House / Spanish Grant
Laird, Iowa Legends (M.A. thesis, State University of Iowa, 1927; HathiTrust iau.31858060747148), McGregor chapter: four family versions collected 1927
tw-ia-north-mcgregor-taylor-gold.t: A 1927 War Department letter to Laird found no record of any lost government sum. One 1927 family version says Dousman hauled the money off on the ice, i.e. it was taken, not lost. Versions place it variously on the bluff N of McGregor, the military-road hilltop, and the Yellow River bottoms near Waukon Junction; no plat read yet, so the pin does not move.
